newsitem.title: GERMANY: Boutros says U.N. not sending peace-keepers to Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Boutros says U.N. not sending peace-keepers to Kabul.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said on Friday the United Nations had no immediate plans to send an interim peace-keeping force to the Afghan capital Kabul but would continue trying to broker peace.

"We are studying the situation now in Kabul and we are thinking about the idea of the demilitarisation of the city," Boutros-Ghali told journalists after presiding over the launch of an international maritime law tribunal in Hamburg.
The U.N. would continue to seek ways to demilitarise the city, which the Taleban militia took three weeks ago, but he stressed all warring parties would have to agree to it.
Ousted government military commander Ahmad Shah Masood urged the Taleban on Friday to quit Kabul and let the U.N. pave the way for all-party talks on a broad-based government.
"Maybe we could be able to send observers there to participate in the ceasefire. But nothing has been decided."
Masood made clear the alternative was war. "If the Taleban are not ready to cooperate with us, we cannot avoid fighting," he told Reuters in Jabal os-Siraj near the Salang Pass.
Boutros-Ghali said all parties would have to accept a peace-keeping force and the Security Council would have to approve it and earmark funds for it.
"For the time being our action must be more a diplomatic action than a military or a paramilitary action," he said.
The U.N. envoy to Afghanistan, German diplomat Norbert Holl, has been negotiating with the different parties since the Taleban seized the capital on September 27.

Taleban fighters brought a measure of peace to areas under its control, but it imposed a fundamentalist version of Islamic observance at variance with Afghanistan's traditionally easy-going Moslem culture.

A Taleban evacuation of Kabul has been floated at the United Nations. The United States called it "probably premature", although State Department spokesman Nicholas Burms said a proposal to demilitarise Kabul was "an important idea".
There was no immediate reaction from the Taleban on Friday, the Moslem day of rest, but they rejected the earlier Masood ultimatum and vowed to defend Kabul.
